stories.title: Give households a cash balance (nal)
stories.i_want: to hold a personal cash balance
stories.so_that: I can buy consumer goods at state-fixed retail prices instead of receiving them for free

acceptance_criteria.text: Every human entity has a nal (cash) balance field that persists across save/load. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; audit §4/§5 confirm humans have no currency field at all, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:37-38]

A citizen's buy order for a consumer good is rejected (or queued/deferred) if their nal balance is below the item's administered retail price, replacing today's unconditional 'purchases resolve on arrival' fulfilment. [SUBSTRATE: CONFLICTS — souls/desire/buyfood.rs:50-54 resolves purchase on arrival with no price param, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:37-38]

stories.title: Pay wages from employer to worker in nal
stories.i_want: to receive a periodic wage in cash from my workplace
stories.so_that: I have money to spend at retail without a free item handout

acceptance_criteria.text: A working human's workplace debits its own account and credits the worker's nal balance on a defined wage interval. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; audit confirms no wages exist, grep for wage/salary returns nothing except a flat government upkeep debit at economy/mod.rs:51, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:17-19]

An unemployed human (no Work.workplace binding) accrues no wage income over any simulated period. [SUBSTRATE: PARTIAL — Work.workplace binding exists (souls/desire/work.rs:20-26) but nothing reads it for money movement today, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:17-19]

stories.title: Give enterprises a separate accounting-rouble (beznal) settlement account
stories.i_want: to settle input purchases and wage payroll from a non-cash accounting account distinct from any household cash
stories.so_that: enterprise-to-enterprise trade and payroll never share a pool with retail consumer spending

acceptance_criteria.text: Every company/enterprise entity carries a beznal balance distinct in type from a citizen's nal balance (not the same undifferentiated Money(i64) scalar reused for both). [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — Money(i64) is one undifferentiated scalar with no account types today, prototypes/src/types/money.rs:14, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:123-125]

Internal (domestic, non-border) trades between enterprises settle in beznal with money_delta no longer hardcoded to zero, replacing today's price-free barter clearing. [SUBSTRATE: CONFLICTS — every internal trade is money_delta: Money::ZERO today, economy/market.rs:226, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:29-31]

stories.title: Forbid beznal from ever buying a consumer good
stories.i_want: a hard rule that enterprise accounting roubles cannot purchase retail consumer goods under any circumstance
stories.so_that: the nal/beznal separation that makes plan fulfilment and shopping queues distinct problems cannot be silently bypassed

acceptance_criteria.text: An attempt to fund a citizen-facing retail purchase from an enterprise's beznal account is rejected at the transaction boundary regardless of balance available, with no code path that converts beznal to nal implicitly. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — no account types or circuit separation exist at all; Money(i64) serves treasury, ext price and trade delta alike with no distinction, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:123-125]

There is no explicit or implicit exchange function that converts a beznal balance into nal outside of the documented wage-payment path (enterprise beznal debit -> worker nal credit is the only legal bridge between circuits). [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, no such boundary exists to violate or preserve yet, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:154-158]

stories.title: Set administered retail prices distinct from enterprise shadow prices
stories.i_want: to set a fixed retail price table for household-facing consumer goods, separate from the enterprise-side ext_value used at the border
stories.so_that: prices never float to clear excess demand — the queue does the clearing instead

acceptance_criteria.text: A retail price table exists per consumer-good item, settable by the player/plan, and is read by every citizen purchase instead of any per-trade computed price. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — no policy layer exists; the only price value is ext_value from calculate_prices, computed once at startup and never recalculated, economy/market.rs:343-403, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:121-122,37]

Setting a retail price and then simulating excess household demand at that price produces a longer queue/wait time and/or empty shelves, never an automatic price increase. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, no queue-vs-price clearing distinction exists in citizen purchase logic today]

Enterprise-facing shadow/settlement prices used for internal beznal trade can differ from the household retail price for the same item, and changing one does not change the other. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; SingleMarket.capital is goods-on-hand not currency and is not a price signal, economy/market.rs:32, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:126-127]

stories.title: Seed a stocked starter warehouse at game start
stories.i_want: a pre-stocked warehouse of essential goods present at turn one
stories.so_that: the very first production chains have something to draw on before any internal chain or import route exists

acceptance_criteria.text: On a new game start, a designated starter warehouse building/store holds a non-zero, config-defined quantity of at least the goods required to bootstrap the opening production chains, before any player action. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, decided 2026-08-22: 'a stocked starter warehouse seeds turn one', docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:159-161]

Goods drawn from the starter warehouse are consumed via the same physical recipe-input path as any other sourced input (Market::buy_until / recipe_init), never a special-cased free-goods branch. [SUBSTRATE: PARTIAL — buy_until always requests exactly item.amount from the static recipe with no distinction of source today, economy/market.rs:161-167, souls/goods_company.rs:23,47, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:142-144]

stories.title: Offer customs imports at a markup as a permanent paid deadlock escape
stories.i_want: to pay a price premium at customs to import a good whenever a domestic supply chain is deadlocked
stories.so_that: a stalled chain always has a costly-but-available way out, distinct from the one-time starter warehouse

acceptance_criteria.text: At any point in the game (not only turn one) the player can place a customs import order for a deficit good at a price strictly higher than its domestic administered/shadow price, and this option remains available for the life of the save. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, decided 2026-08-22: 'customs imports at a markup remain the permanent paid escape hatch whenever a chain deadlocks', docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:159-161]

A customs import order debits the treasury's hard-currency (foreign rouble) account, never the enterprise beznal or household nal circuits, distinguishing this from internal trade. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; today the only money pool at all is Government.money and it is undifferentiated, economy/government.rs:10, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:127-128]

The markup import does not resolve instantly: it still requires the same physical border-clearance and inland haul as any other foreign trade order (see border-crossing story), it is not a same-tick money-for-goods shortcut. [SUBSTRATE: CONFLICTS — today every unmet buy order is satisfied instantly and unconditionally by an infinite external partner with no vehicle trip, economy/market.rs:285-304, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:130-135]

stories.title: Require a physical vehicle trip to move goods across the border
stories.i_want: an ordered import/export to remain unfulfilled until a vehicle physically hauls the goods across a customs building
stories.so_that: money at the border is never sufficient by itself — the one rule that nothing teleports holds at the border too

acceptance_criteria.text: Placing a foreign trade order does not immediately mutate any goods quantity or capital field; goods only appear/disappear from domestic stock after a vehicle entity completes a trip through a border-crossing building. [SUBSTRATE: CONFLICTS — today external buy/sell loops mutate capital in the same tick with no vehicle trip at all, economy/market.rs:285-304 (buy side), :307-331 (sell side), docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:130-135]

If no freight/vehicle capacity exists to service a foreign trade order, the order remains queued and no capital or money changes hands — replacing today's behaviour where capital is credited before existence of a freight station is even checked. [SUBSTRATE: CONFLICTS — confirmed bug: both external loops mutate capital before checking a freight station exists (market.rs:291 credits, :293 checks; symmetric at :317/:320); if find_external returns None goods appear with no trade record and no money debit, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:136-141]

Foreign trade throughput is capped by physical means (customs bay count, fleet size, border-edge capacity) rather than by any numeric trade-volume token, so a saturated customs house measurably slows import/export rate. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; no vehicle-bay or throughput model exists at the border today, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:130-135]

stories.title: Build customs houses as typed border-crossing buildings
stories.i_want: to construct a customs house with a transport mode (road/rail/air), a per-cargo-class buffer, vehicle bays, and both a domestic-facing and a border-facing edge
stories.so_that: foreign trade has a physical building the player sites and can bottleneck, not an implicit map-edge shop

acceptance_criteria.text: A customs house is a placeable building entity distinct from ordinary production buildings, with fields for mode, per-transport-class buffer (1-unit buffer per cargo class), bay list, domestic edge, and border edge. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; no BorderCrossing/customs building type exists in the codebase, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:130-135 (external partner has no building at all)]

There is no map-edge 'infinite external partner' reachable without passing through a built customs house — every export/import order resolves only via a player-built or pre-placed customs house entity. [SUBSTRATE: CONFLICTS — today the external partner exists with no capacity limit and is reachable with no building constructed, economy/market.rs:285-331, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:130-135]

Electricity import/export transformers and border pipelines exist as separate typed border-crossing endpoints from road/rail/air customs houses, with the transport medium of a good deciding which border building it crosses at (the same routing rule used domestically). [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; no utility border building type exists, only a road/rail/air customs house concept is modelled at all, spec/trade.md:14-15]

A customs house may be either a pre-placed/map-provided instance or a player-constructed instance (the `$SUBTYPE_OWN_CUSTOM` distinction), and both variants participate in border trade identically once built. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; no customs house entity exists yet to have this ownership distinction, spec/trade.md:13]

stories.title: Settle foreign trade only on physical border clearance
stories.i_want: treasury debit/credit for a trade to occur at the moment the vehicle clears the border, not at order-match time
stories.so_that: treasury and simulation state never diverge

acceptance_criteria.text: A trade order's status progresses ordered -> atCustoms -> cleared, and the treasury balance changes only on the transition into cleared, never earlier. [SUBSTRATE: CONFLICTS — settlement happens at match time today (the same tick the pair is drained in make_trades), not at any border-clearance event, economy/market.rs:193-336, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:130-135]

If a save is loaded mid-transit (a trade order in the atCustoms state), the treasury balance on load reflects only cleared trades, and the in-flight order resumes without double-crediting or losing the goods. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; no in-flight trade state or save-compatible representation of it exists today, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:130-135]

(OPEN/DEFERRED — whether a trade order locks its price at order time or floats to the clearance-time price is an undecided design question per spec/trade.md:57,63, not scheduled for 1.0 until resolved) A trade order's price-snapshot policy is not yet defined; the draft data model reserves an optional `priceAtOrder?` field for whichever policy is later chosen. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; no policy decision or field exists in code, spec/trade.md:57,63]

A cleared trade's paired ledger entry is tagged as import or export at settlement, enabling per-direction trade-balance reporting distinct from a currency-only or amount-only record. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; no ledger entry type distinguishes import/export direction today, spec/trade.md:26]

stories.title: Track two hard-currency ledgers, roubles and dollars
stories.i_want: domestic-bloc trade to settle in roubles and hard-currency trade to settle in dollars, in two separate treasury balances with no free conversion
stories.so_that: being rouble-rich does not automatically mean I can buy Western goods

acceptance_criteria.text: Treasury carries two distinct currency balances (roubles, dollars); a good's trade currency is a property of the good/origin, not a runtime player choice. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — Government.money is a single undifferentiated Money(i64) scalar today, economy/government.rs:10, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:123-128]

There is no direct rouble-to-dollar conversion action; dollars are obtainable only via export settlement or a dollar-denominated loan. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, exchange rate/conversion mechanic explicitly flagged as an open gap in trade.md's own evidence log]

stories.title: Offer per-currency loans with interest and borrowing caps
stories.i_want: to borrow roubles or dollars separately, each with its own interest rate, penalty rate, and borrowing cap
stories.so_that: debt pressure is currency-specific, matching the two-ledger split the rest of foreign trade already enforces

acceptance_criteria.text: (DEFERRED to Post-1.0 per docs/charter-1.0.md:108 — captured, not scheduled for 1.0) Treasury supports a loan per currency, each carrying its own principal, interest rate, and penalty rate, matching the `loans: [{currency, principal, rate, penaltyRate}]` shape in the design draft. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; no loan mechanic or Treasury type exists at all, spec/trade.md:22-23,53]

stories.title: Let the plan set standing import/export contracts fulfilled by logistics
stories.i_want: the plan to set standing import/export contracts (quotas) rather than negotiate every shipment order manually
stories.so_that: foreign trade quotas are a plan artifact and logistics dispatch fulfils them physically, consistent with domestic deficit-driven dispatch

acceptance_criteria.text: A standing import or export contract set by the plan specifies a good, a quantity/quota, and a direction, and logistics dispatch fulfils it over time via the same physical border-crossing path as any other trade order, rather than requiring the player to place a fresh order for every shipment. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; no plan-contract or quota mechanism exists, spec/trade.md:60-61]

stories.title: Gate the import/export catalogue by era and bloc
stories.i_want: which goods and vehicles are importable/exportable to change with the campaign timeline and bloc alignment
stories.so_that: trade is a geopolitical lever, not a static shop

acceptance_criteria.text: Each tradeable item/vehicle prototype carries an availability window (era range) and an origin/bloc tag, and an order for an item outside its current availability window or bloc alignment is rejected at customs. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — ItemPrototype today is only {base, id, optout_exttrade}, no era or country fields exist, prototypes/src/prototypes/item.rs:8-12, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:47-48]

stories.title: Depreciate exported vehicles by condition on resale
stories.i_want: an exported vehicle's sale value to depend on its wear/condition, not just its base price
stories.so_that: players cannot churn new vehicles across the border for free money

acceptance_criteria.text: Exporting a used vehicle yields strictly less hard currency than exporting an equivalent new vehicle, as a function of a tracked condition/wear value. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; Vehicle is a bare kinematic shell today with no wear/condition/owner economic fields at all, transportation/vehicle.rs:34-44, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:22]

stories.title: Publish the world-market price model to the player
stories.i_want: to see the current export/import price of each traded good and the drivers moving it (era, world events, my own export volume)
stories.so_that: the moving market is legible rather than a black box

acceptance_criteria.text: A player-facing view shows, for a traded item, its current border price and at least the named drivers that changed it since the last check. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; the only price value that exists is ext_value, a fixed per-item value computed once at startup and never recalculated or exposed as a curve, economy/market.rs:35, calculate_prices at market.rs:343-403, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:121-122]

The border price for a good changes over simulated time in response to at least one modelled driver (e.g. cumulative export volume), rather than remaining the single startup-computed constant it is today. [SUBSTRATE: CONFLICTS — ext_value from calculate_prices is computed once, never recalculated, economy/market.rs:343-403, docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md:37-38,121-122]

scenarios.title: New game starts with a stocked starter warehouse
preconditions: Fresh new-game start, no player actions taken yet

steps.action: Load a new game
expected: Simulation initializes without error

steps.action: Inspect the starter warehouse's stock
expected: Warehouse holds the configured non-zero starting quantities of bootstrap goods

final_observables: Starter warehouse stock matches the configured seed quantities before any tick advances
owning_story_titles: Seed a stocked starter warehouse at game start

scenarios.title: Deadlocked domestic chain is broken by a marked-up customs import
preconditions: A production chain has zero domestic supply of a required input and no path to acquire it internally (simulated deadlock)

steps.action: Player places a customs import order for the deficit good
expected: Order is accepted and priced above the domestic administered/shadow price

steps.action: Advance simulation until a vehicle completes the border-to-inland haul
expected: Treasury's foreign-currency balance is debited only at the moment of physical clearance, not at order time

steps.action: Advance the deadlocked chain
expected: Chain resumes production using the imported goods

final_observables: Deadlocked chain produces output again
Treasury foreign-currency balance decreased by the markup price
No enterprise beznal or household nal balance changed
owning_story_titles: Offer customs imports at a markup as a permanent paid deadlock escape
Settle foreign trade only on physical border clearance

scenarios.title: Foreign trade order stalls with no vehicle capacity, no money moves
preconditions: A foreign trade order is placed
No freight vehicle/fleet capacity exists to service the customs house

steps.action: Advance the simulation for many ticks with no freight capacity available
expected: Order remains in the ordered or atCustoms state, never reaches cleared

final_observables: No capital/goods quantity changed for either party
No treasury balance changed
Order is still visibly queued to the player, not silently dropped
owning_story_titles: Require a physical vehicle trip to move goods across the border

scenarios.title: Household cash cannot be spent using enterprise accounting roubles
preconditions: An enterprise holds a beznal balance sufficient to cover a retail good's price
A citizen's nal balance is zero

steps.action: Attempt to fund the citizen's retail purchase directly from the enterprise's beznal account (bypassing wages)
expected: Transaction is rejected

final_observables: Citizen does not receive the good
Enterprise beznal balance is unchanged
No implicit beznal-to-nal conversion occurred
owning_story_titles: Forbid beznal from ever buying a consumer good

scenarios.title: Excess retail demand lengthens the queue instead of raising the price
preconditions: Administered retail price for a good is set and held fixed
Household demand for the good exceeds current shelf stock

steps.action: Advance simulation with demand continuing to exceed stock
expected: Retail price for the good is unchanged tick over tick

final_observables: Queue length and/or wait time for the good has increased
Administered price is bit-for-bit identical to before the demand spike
owning_story_titles: Set administered retail prices distinct from enterprise shadow prices

scenarios.title: Treasury and simulation stay consistent across a mid-transit save/load
preconditions: A foreign trade order has been matched and is in the atCustoms (in-transit) state, not yet cleared

steps.action: Save the game
expected: Save completes without error

steps.action: Reload the save
expected: Order is restored in the atCustoms state

steps.action: Advance simulation until the vehicle clears the border
expected: Treasury is credited/debited exactly once, at clearance

final_observables: Treasury balance after clearance equals pre-save balance plus/minus exactly one trade's value
No double-settlement and no lost settlement occurred
owning_story_titles: Settle foreign trade only on physical border clearance

scenarios.title: Dollar-only good cannot be bought with a rouble-only balance
preconditions: Treasury holds a large rouble balance and zero dollars
Target import good is tagged as a hard-currency (dollar) good

steps.action: Attempt to place an import order for the dollar-tagged good
expected: Order is rejected or blocked pending dollar funds

final_observables: Rouble balance is unchanged
No goods are imported
owning_story_titles: Track two hard-currency ledgers, roubles and dollars

scenarios.title: Household nal balance persists across save and load
preconditions: A citizen holds a non-zero nal balance

steps.action: Save the game
expected: Save completes without error

steps.action: Reload the save
expected: Citizen's nal balance is restored to the exact pre-save value

final_observables: Citizen nal balance after load equals nal balance before save

scenarios.title: Wage payment debits employer beznal and credits worker nal on interval
preconditions: A human is bound to a workplace via Work.workplace
Both the workplace's beznal balance and the worker's nal balance are known before the wage interval elapses

steps.action: Advance simulation past one wage interval
expected: Workplace beznal balance decreases by the wage amount
Worker nal balance increases by the same wage amount

final_observables: Worker nal balance increased exactly by the wage amount
Workplace beznal balance decreased by the same amount
No other account's balance changed
owning_story_titles: Pay wages from employer to worker in nal

scenarios.title: Domestic enterprise-to-enterprise trade settles in beznal with a nonzero delta
preconditions: Two domestic enterprises complete an internal (non-border) trade of goods

steps.action: Advance simulation until the internal trade resolves
expected: Buyer's beznal balance decreases by a nonzero money_delta
Seller's beznal balance increases by the same nonzero money_delta

final_observables: money_delta for the trade is nonzero, not the current Money::ZERO barter clearing
Neither party's nal balance changed
owning_story_titles: Give enterprises a separate accounting-rouble (beznal) settlement account

scenarios.title: Building a customs house creates a placeable border-crossing entity
preconditions: Player has access to the build menu

steps.action: Place a customs house building
expected: Building entity is created with mode, per-class buffer, bay list, domestic edge, and border edge fields populated

final_observables: A customs house entity exists distinct from ordinary production buildings
owning_story_titles: Build customs houses as typed border-crossing buildings

scenarios.title: Foreign trade order cannot resolve with no customs house built
preconditions: No customs house has been built on the map
A foreign trade order is placed

steps.action: Advance simulation for many ticks with no customs house built
expected: Order never reaches cleared
No goods or money move for either party

final_observables: No infinite external partner services the order
Order remains unfulfilled until a customs house is built
owning_story_titles: Build customs houses as typed border-crossing buildings

scenarios.title: Import order outside its era/bloc window is rejected at customs
preconditions: An item's availability window and bloc tag are set
Current game era or player's bloc alignment falls outside that item's window/tag

steps.action: Place an import/export order for the out-of-window or out-of-bloc item
expected: Order is rejected at customs

final_observables: No goods or money moved for the rejected order
Item remains unavailable until era/bloc conditions are met
owning_story_titles: Gate the import/export catalogue by era and bloc

scenarios.title: Used vehicle export fetches less hard currency than an equivalent new vehicle
preconditions: Two otherwise-identical vehicles exist, one new (full condition) and one worn (reduced condition)

steps.action: Export the new vehicle
expected: Hard currency credited equals the vehicle's full base price

steps.action: Export the worn vehicle
expected: Hard currency credited is strictly less than the full base price

final_observables: Worn vehicle's export payout is strictly less than the new vehicle's export payout for the same prototype
owning_story_titles: Depreciate exported vehicles by condition on resale

scenarios.title: Player-facing view shows a price move and its driver
preconditions: A traded good's border price changes due to a modelled driver (e.g. cumulative export volume)

steps.action: Trigger the driver (e.g. export enough volume to move the price)
expected: Border price for the good changes

steps.action: Open the player-facing price view for that good
expected: View shows the new price and names the driver that changed it

final_observables: Displayed price matches the current border price
At least one named driver is shown alongside the price
owning_story_titles: Publish the world-market price model to the player
